body:
If `instant` is set to false, the search is only triggered if ENTER is pressed.
- Added some tests on even registration
- Removed an outdated version of the searchbox that was at the root level of the widgets/ directory.
- Updated jsdoc

Fix #458

comments.body: I like the feature but I am unsure about `instant` API option. The library is called "instantsearch" but we have an option to disable the "instant": it was my first reaction.
Along with this option we would need a `submit` button to be generated (as an option too), because otherwise it makes sense only on desktop

> I like the feature but I am unsure about instant API option. The library is called "instantsearch" but we have an option to disable the "instant": it was my first reaction.

Any idea what could be a better naming? `searchAsYouType: true/false` was not nice :/

> Along with this option we would need a submit button to be generated (as an option too), because otherwise it makes sense only on desktop

Hmmm, it is the goal responsibility of the searchbox? Because having a submit button means you have a wrapping `<form>` as well. Good point but not sure how to fix it :/

> Hmmm, it is the goal responsibility of the searchbox? Because having a submit button means you have a wrapping <form> as well. Good point but not sure how to fix it :/

Well we can have a wrapping form or not, that's not mandatory. You can add just a button type submit and handle the submit on it. Or we can have a wrapping form, we have one for example in the priceRanges widget.

But that's for later

> Any idea what could be a better naming? searchAsYouType: true/false was not nice :/

`searchOnEnterKeyPressOnly` exhaustive he!

Sorry I'm late, but as @vvo asked, why do we need that? Shouldn't we push the instant search as the only real way to do intuitive search? I feel like integration this small option (which is in opposition with the main goal of the library) will create an large array of side effects.

title: feat(searchBox): ability to be non-instant
